generationContext.text:
# Azure Event Grid client library for .NET

Azure Event Grid allows you to easily build applications with event-based architectures. The Event Grid service fully manages all routing of events from any source, to any destination, for any application. Azure service events and custom events can be published directly to the service, where the events can then be filtered and sent to various recipients, such as built-in handlers or custom webhooks. To learn more about Azure Event Grid: [What is Event Grid?](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/overview)

Use the client library for Azure Event Grid to:
- Publish events to Event Grid topics using the Cloud Event schema
- Consume and settle events

  [Source code](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/eventgrid/Azure.Messaging.EventGrid.Namespaces/src) | [Package (NuGet)](https://www.nuget.org/packages) | [API reference documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/overview/azure/messaging.eventgrid-readme?view=azure-dotnet) | [Product documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/pull-delivery-overview) | [Samples](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/tree/main/sdk/eventgrid/Azure.Messaging.EventGrid.Namespaces/samples)

## Getting started

### Install the package

Install the client library for .NET with [NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/ ):

```dotnetcli
dotnet add package Azure.Messaging.EventGrid.Namespaces
```

### Prerequisites

You must have an [Azure subscription](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/dotnet/) and an Azure resource group with a custom Event Grid topic or domain. Follow this [step-by-step tutorial](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/custom-event-quickstart-portal) to register the Event Grid resource provider and create Event Grid topics using the [Azure portal](https://portal.azure.com/). There is a [similar tutorial](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/custom-event-quickstart) using [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure).

### Authenticate the client

In order for the client library to interact with a topic or domain, you will need the `endpoint` of the Event Grid topic and a `credential`, which can be created using the topic's access key.

You can find the endpoint for your Event Grid topic either in the [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com/) or by using the [Azure CLI](https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure) snippet below.

```bash
az eventgrid topic show --name <your-resource-name> --resource-group <your-resource-group-name> --query "endpoint"
```

The access key can also be found through the [portal](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/event-grid/get-access-keys), or by using the Azure CLI snippet below:
```bash
az eventgrid topic key list --name <your-resource-name> --resource-group <your-resource-group-name> --query "key1"
```

#### Authenticate using Topic Access Key

Once you have your access key and topic endpoint, you can create the publisher client as follows:
```C# Snippet:CreateNamespaceClient
// Construct the client using an Endpoint for a namespace as well as the shared access key
var senderClient = new EventGridSenderClient(new Uri(namespaceTopicHost), topicName, new AzureKeyCredential(namespaceKey));
```

#### Authenticate using an Entra ID

Azure Event Grid provides integration with Entra ID for identity-based authentication of requests. With Entra ID, you can use role-based access control (RBAC) to grant access to your Azure Event Grid resources to users, groups, or applications. The [Azure Identity library](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/tree/main/sdk/identity/Azure.Identity/README.md) provides easy Azure Active Directory support for authentication.

To send events to a topic or domain using Azure Active Directory, the authenticated identity should have the "EventGrid Data Sender" role assigned.

```C# Snippet:CreateNamespaceClientAAD
// Construct the sender client using an Endpoint for a namespace as well as the DefaultAzureCredential
var senderClient = new EventGridSenderClient(new Uri(namespaceTopicHost), topicName, new DefaultAzureCredential());
```

## Key concepts

### Thread safety

We guarantee that all client instance methods are thread-safe and independent of each other ([guideline](https://azure.github.io/azure-sdk/dotnet_introduction.html#dotnet-service-methods-thread-safety)). This ensures that the recommendation of reusing client instances is always safe, even across threads.

## Examples

You can familiarize yourself with different APIs using [Samples](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/tree/main/sdk/eventgrid/Azure.Messaging.EventGrid.Namespaces/samples).

## Troubleshooting

Describe common errors and exceptions, how to "unpack" them if necessary, and include guidance for graceful handling and recovery.

Provide information to help developers avoid throttling or other service-enforced errors they might encounter. For example, provide guidance and examples for using retry or connection policies in the API.

If the package or a related package supports it, include tips for logging or enabling instrumentation to help them debug their code.

## Next steps

View more https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/eventgrid/Azure.Messaging.EventGrid.Namespaces/samples here for common usages of the Event Grid client library: [Event Grid Samples](https://github.com/Azure/azure-sdk-for-net/blob/main/sdk/eventgrid/Azure.Messaging.EventGrid.Namespaces/samples).

decisions.reason: AcknowledgeResult.cs lines 11-20 implement the stated null-preserving JSON RequestContent cast in a partial type outside Generated. The pattern describes a reusable model-to-request-content conversion; emitting such conversions is plausibly generator-addressable.
BrokerProperties.cs lines 12-21 independently implement the stated implicit conversion, including the null case and WireOptions, in the handwritten customization partial.

BrokerProperties.cs lines 24-29 show the explicit Response conversion, disposal of the response and JsonDocument, and deserialization with WireOptions; this is separate from its request-content conversion.

The handwritten CodeGenType mapping and internal accessibility are explicit, and sender overloads use CloudEvent rather than CloudEventInternal. The supplied code does not independently identify the assembly that defines the public CloudEvent, so the explanation should not assert its provenance as a verified fact.

finding.explanation: CodeGenType maps the generated CloudEvent to an internal CloudEventInternal; handwritten sender overloads instead take CloudEvent parameters.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The CodeGenType mapping and internal partial declaration are outside src/Generated, and the sender partial declares the alternative public parameter type.

decisions.reason: The explicit CodeGenType mapping changes a generated factory's name, despite its empty body. This is a rename, not replacement of a model with another type; use a factory-renaming pattern and a subtype reflecting the type rather than a model instance.

finding.explanation: CodeGenType maps AzureMessagingEventGridNamespacesModelFactory to the public EventGridNamespacesModelFactory name.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The non-generated partial's CodeGenType attribute changes the generated type's name even though its body is empty.

decisions.reason: BuilderExtensions.cs lines 20-66 contain four handwritten registration overloads for the two clients, using explicit key credentials or the credential supplied by the builder. Client-builder registration is a reusable generation candidate, though no generator implementation is provided.

BuilderExtensions.cs lines 71-87 independently add configuration-based registrations for sender and receiver, with the stated trimming and dynamic-code attributes; the pattern names their reusable configuration-registration shape.

ReceiverClient.cs lines 18-23 suppress generated constructors; lines 92-137 replace them with validation, key-header/bearer authentication pipelines, and stored topic/subscription. The category and credential-specific pipeline pattern match the distinct construction behavior.

ReceiverClient.cs lines 33-57 contain both the optional-policy internal pipeline constructor and the experimental settings constructor that forwards endpoint/options; the matching suppressions appear at lines 22-23. No claim is made that settings populate the stored topic/subscription.

The cited receiver methods are indeed handwritten topic/subscription-bound forwarding overloads, but the proposed typed-wrapper pattern misclassifies protocol overloads accepting RequestContent/RequestContext. The supplied excerpt ends before the synchronous protocol Release overload.

finding.explanation: Typed and protocol receiver overloads forward stored topic and subscription names into the corresponding operations, removing those arguments from the covered caller-facing methods.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The forwarding overload bodies are in EventGridReceiverClient.cs under src/Customization rather than Generated.

decisions.reason: ReceiverClientOptions.cs lines 12-38 define the service-version enum, default, two wire strings, and unsupported-value exception outside Generated. The version-curation pattern is reusable and can plausibly be addressed at generation time.
Settings.cs lines 11 and 16 suppress and replace Options with a receiver-specific options type. This is a member type replacement, not an alias property.

finding.explanation: CodeGenSuppress removes the generated Options member and the handwritten partial declares a settable EventGridReceiverClientOptions member.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The explicit CodeGenSuppress attribute and replacement member are in src/Customization.

decisions.reason: Settings.cs lines 12 and 20-26 show a handwritten binding override that conditionally parses the configured Endpoint as an absolute Uri. BindCore is protected configuration behavior, not a public convenience method; the snippet does not establish why this override was needed.

finding.explanation: A replacement BindCore reads Endpoint from the configuration section and sets it only if Uri.TryCreate parses an absolute Uri.
finding.handwrittenRationale: CodeGenSuppress for BindCore and its non-generated override body explicitly replace generated settings binding.

decisions.reason: SenderClient.cs lines 18-23 suppress the generated constructors and lines 90-133 implement both key-header and bearer-token construction, including topic validation and tracing-option storage. Credential-specific pipeline construction is the reusable behavior.
SenderClient.cs lines 33-57 independently implement optional-policy pipeline construction and an experimental settings overload, corresponding to constructor suppressions at lines 22-23.

SenderClient.cs lines 139-207 implement sync/async single and batch CloudEvent overloads using CloudEventRequestContent or CloudEventsRequestContent, the tracing option, and the stored topic. The methods are outside Generated, and a typed wrapper is the applicable reusable shape.

SenderClient.cs lines 229-337 implement four handwritten RequestContent protocol overloads, hide them from normal editor browsing, and forward the stored topic. The SendEvent pair also adds validation and named diagnostic scopes, separately covered by the tracing proposal.

SenderClient.cs lines 171-206 and 234-284 explicitly create/start named scopes, mark exceptions failed and rethrow in both batch typed sends and single protocol sends. This is separate tracing behavior from the forwarding/serialization wrappers.

SenderClient.cs lines 339-348 define a handwritten helper that returns a shared default RequestContext for noncancelable tokens and otherwise creates one carrying the token; sender methods call it at lines 143, 157, 169 and 193. The reusable shape could plausibly be generated for methods accepting CancellationToken.

limitations: Evidence includes ten files from a partial scan; receiver source ends at line 329 inside protocol Release documentation. No claims are made about unseen reject/renew operations or the rest of the receiver.

Sender options/settings, several result customizations and shared CloudEvent(s)RequestContent implementations are omitted. Passing the tracing flag is visible but its serialization or tracing injection implementation is not.
AuthorizationHeader, AuthorizationApiKeyPrefix and AuthorizationScopes definitions are not supplied; the policy wiring is visible, not their exact values.

EventGridNamespacesClientOptions has only an internal empty partial declaration without an explicit generator attribute or generated counterpart. Its accessibility change is not substantiated enough to count independently.

Generated neighbors are absent. The options-version finding follows the supplied .NET non-generated-source rule, which the guideline itself labels proposed; explicit attributes provide stronger evidence for the other mapped/suppressed members.
No paging or LRO behavior is inferred from event receive/release operations or documentation.

Coverage is partial: 10 of 84 eligible files were captured; EventGridReceiverClient.cs stops at line 329, and the listed sender options/settings and result files were not supplied. No absence inference is possible outside the provided snippets.

Generated partials and linked shared CloudEventRequestContent implementations are not supplied, so the exact generated signatures, the CloudEvent defining assembly, and the serialization or tracing behavior inside shared content types cannot be independently verified.

The experimental settings constructors initialize a pipeline without setting the topic/subscription fields shown in the ordinary client constructors; the supplied snippets do not establish how callers configure or use those settings-backed clients. No additional independent finding is asserted from that uncertainty.
